title: Docs: streaming guide parity update (events, disconnect handling, timeouts)
author: Wei Chen
description:
This updates the streaming guide to match the SDK parity standard across Python/TypeScript/Go. Key changes: (1) document standardized streaming event semantics, including where `request_id` appears and what is guaranteed to be delivered; (2) add explicit guidance for disconnects/partial output and safe retry patterns (idempotency); (3) align recommended timeout configuration for streaming vs non-streaming requests; (4) add a proxy/corporate network troubleshooting section (buffering/half-closed connections) based on recent support cases.

Why:
- We’ve had multiple reports of inconsistent behavior across SDKs (timeouts not honored in Python streaming, unclear disconnect semantics behind proxies, and missing request_id in surfaced errors). These docs need to reflect the standardized behavior landing in the SDK releases.

Scope:
- Docs only (no API changes). References the retry/timeout standard + ADRs and uses the same naming as the SDKs.

Notable doc updates:
- “Streaming events” section now treats the stream as an ordered sequence of events with clear invariants:
  - You may receive a partial response before a terminal error (disconnect / timeout / cancellation).
  - The SDK surfaces `request_id` on both success and error paths; the guide shows how to log it.
  - Terminal states: normal completion vs client cancellation vs transport disconnect.
- “Disconnect handling” section clarifies what to do when the connection drops mid-stream:
  - Do not blindly retry streaming requests unless you can tolerate duplicates.
  - Prefer application-level idempotency and logging (`request_id`, attempt count) when retrying.
- “Timeouts” section aligns recommended values across languages and distinguishes:
  - Connect timeout (recommended 10s)
  - Overall timeout (recommended 60s non-streaming)
  - Streaming timeout guidance (recommended overall 5m for typical interactive chat streams; shorter for server-side tools/agents that may hang; always pair with explicit cancellation).
- “Retries” section aligns with parity behavior:
  - Retried for 429/5xx and transient network errors for non-streaming.
  - Streaming is conservative: no automatic replay after receiving any stream bytes; the SDK will raise a typed streaming error that includes `request_id` and whether partial output was returned.

Related:
- SDK parity epic: ENG-5120
- Error taxonomy alignment: ENG-5126
- Support drivers: SUP-29505, SUP-29410
- Docs retries/timeouts alignment PR: redwood-docs#3921

Screenshots: N/A (text-only changes)

Checklist:
- [x] Uses consistent option names across Python/TS/Go examples
- [x] Includes request_id logging example
- [x] Mentions Retry-After / 429 behavior (non-streaming)
- [x] Clarifies streaming retry constraints and idempotency guidance
- [x] Reviewed by SDK parity tech lead + SRE for timeout guidance wording

review_conversation: Elliot Price (review) 2026-02-11: This is the right direction. Two nits: (1) Can we avoid implying the server guarantees exactly-once delivery for streamed tokens? (2) Add a short callout that corporate proxies may buffer SSE and increase perceived latency.

Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-11: Updated wording to “best-effort ordered delivery over a single connection” and added a proxy buffering callout with common symptoms (tokens arrive in bursts, sudden FIN mid-chunk).

Ibrahim Khan (review) 2026-02-12: Please make the streaming retry guidance explicit: if any bytes have been received, SDKs will not auto-retry the request. Also add a note that retries after disconnect require app-level idempotency to prevent duplicated side effects.

Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-12: Added a “When NOT to retry” subsection + explicit statement about no auto-retry after receiving stream bytes. Included idempotency guidance and pointed to the examples PR that shows idempotency keys + request_id logging.

Allison Grant (review) 2026-02-13: Timeout section: recommend concrete defaults and differentiate connect vs overall vs streaming. Also: avoid suggesting infinite timeouts; we want explicit cancellation to prevent hung reads.

Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-13: Updated with recommended values: connect=10s; overall(non-stream)=60s; overall(streaming)=5m as a starting point; and added “always set an upper bound + cancellation” guidance. Removed any implication of infinite timeouts.

Sabrina James (review) 2026-02-14: Python snippet: please show cancellation and catching the typed streaming disconnect error (and logging request_id). Also ensure we don’t print tokens that might include secrets in the troubleshooting example.

Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-14: Updated Python snippet to demonstrate cancellation + catching the streaming error type and logging only request_id + error code. Troubleshooting section now recommends redacting content and avoiding debug logs in production.

Dana Lo (review) 2026-02-15: TS snippet: use AbortController and show how to stop iteration on cancel. Also rename the event fields in the example to match the SDK after PR-1311 (message_start/token/message_end).
Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-15: Updated TS snippet to use AbortController and updated event names/shape to match the latest parity spec.

Mateusz Zielinski (review) 2026-02-16: Go snippet: show context cancellation + ensure we demonstrate reading until EOF vs error. Also please add a one-liner: if you see frequent disconnects behind proxies, try shorter idle timeouts and/or switch networks to isolate.
Wei Chen (author) 2026-02-16: Added context cancellation example and a short troubleshooting note about isolating proxy/network behavior and tuning idle/read timeouts.
Ibrahim Khan (approve) 2026-02-18: Approved. Matches the parity standard and avoids overstating retry behavior.
Elliot Price (approve) 2026-02-18: Approved. Good customer-facing clarity; thanks for tightening the reliability language.
release_notes: Docs only: updated streaming guide to reflect standardized SDK streaming semantics (events, disconnect handling, recommended timeouts, and conservative streaming retry guidance).
